cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 47th District since January 2025. Previously a California state senator (2020–2024), UC Irvine law professor, SEC enforcement attorney, counsel to Sen. Chuck Schumer, and policy director at the Center for American Progress. Harvard Law graduate; lives in Irvine.

controversies.text: Federal records show United Democracy Project, AIPAC's super PAC, spent $4,615,289 to oppose them since 2021.
Missed 2 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.3%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 1, 2025-03-27 to 2025-03-27.

Police stopped Min in Sacramento on May 2, 2023 and arrested him on suspicion of drunk driving. In August 2023 he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor DUI. He got two days in jail, three months in a first-offender program and three years of informal probation. After the arrest he said, "My decision to drive last night was irresponsible."

endorsements.text: 2026: California Democratic Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

2024: Los Angeles Times editorial board, Planned Parenthood, League of Conservation Voters, and the Fraternal Order of Police, plus the Los Angeles Police Protective League and Association for Los Angeles Deputy Sheriffs.
His campaign site says he is endorsed by the California Democratic Party, California Labor Federation, Planned Parenthood Action, Sierra Club and the Brady Campaign to End Gun Violence.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance by Min on data centers or on local development projects. We also found no records of his actions or statements on statewide data-center limits, homestead property-tax relief, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, or H-1B visas. We found no statement from him pledging to refuse corporate, PAC or other big-donor money. The page for his 2026 positions on housing and public safety was cut off, so those issues are left out. Details of the state-level bills he authored beyond what is summarized above could not be checked, and the Ballotpedia section on the 2023 arrest was not in the text we could read.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2018 campaign he said he opposes using taxpayer money to fund private schools, including charter schools and vouchers, and that federal education money should not be tied to school-choice requirements. The same page shows he supports increased federal education investment.

pro-life.evidence: He supports federal legislation protecting abortion rights, and in a 2023 Ballotpedia survey he said he authored a proposition to add abortion and contraception access to the California Constitution.

second-amendment.evidence: As a state senator, he authored the law banning gun shows at the Orange County Fairgrounds and other state-owned property.

workers-first.evidence: He voted against a Republican immigration bill that would make sexual and domestic violence offenses deportable, saying it would have a chilling effect on victims reporting crimes.

back-police-order.evidence: In September 2025 he voted for two Republican bills strengthening juvenile sentencing in Washington, D.C., and against a third bill on police pursuits there.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: As a state senator he authored California's '30 by 30' land-conservation bill, signed by Gov. Newsom in 2023.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 6 priorities; 4 backed by their record, 0 only promised

cands.bio: Republican business executive and strategist. Former Bain consultant, co-founder of two startups, business owner, and managing director of Management Consulted. Author. Ran for California governor in 2021 and 2022. Candidate for U.S. House District 47 in 2026. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed on Ballotpedia as a 2026 endorsement)
Reform California (listed on Ballotpedia as a 2026 endorsement)

cands.gaps: We could not find where she grew up, when she moved to California, or where she lives now. We found no stated positions from her 2026 House campaign, since she did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey. Her stated positions come from her 2021 and 2022 campaigns for governor. We found nothing on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, guns, abortion, immigration or H-1B, or teacher pay. We found no record of governing or legislative work, because she has held no office. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond those listed.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In a 2021 Ballotpedia survey (governor race), she said state funding should follow the student to public, charter, private or homeschool, and that she would expand charter options for children in low-performing schools. back-police-order.evidence: Her 2022 governor campaign website said she would support pay increases for police and work to retain and hire officers. It also said she would stop prison closures.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In 2021 and 2022 governor-race materials, she said she would reform CEQA to streamline housing, streamline regulatory approvals and development impact fees, and incentivize localities to simplify growth ordinances.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In her 2021 Ballotpedia survey (governor race), she said she would reform the California Environmental Quality Act to streamline the building of more housing units, while saying the environment can still be protected.
Her 2022 governor campaign website said she would streamline regulatory approvals and development impact fees, and tie future homelessness funding to annual building-permit targets.
